Commentary.Commentary: After a long time in the sun, the hosts look to be a spent force and they will now get a much-needed break. On the contrary, Zimbabwe's bowlers look like they are wearing down, struggling to get some bounce and pace from the wicket. The weight of his 40 plus overs hanging heavy on him, Cremer is not looking as spry as before. The bowlers have been making a great effort to get wickets but to no avail, with the exception of Chinouya. They have been leaking runs and not able to get the wickets. New Zealand is looking very well settled in but the Lunch break might give the hosts time to recuperate and come back stronger. Join us at 1540 IST for the 2nd session.

This innings has belonged solely to the Kiwis. They have not obliged the hosts efforts and have stuck around at the crease and continued to pile on the runs at a steady pace. Early in the day, the nightwatchman Sodhi was dismissed by Chinouya but he had already done his job and that was the only moment of weakness for New Zealand. Taylor remained steady and has gone on to score 87. Watling has played a good supporting role as well, scoring his own half-century just before lunch and bringing up a 100-run partnership. They have showing no signs of slowing down.

Hello and welcome to day 3 of the Test between Zimbabwe and New Zealand. Yesterday, we saw some decent cricket as the Kiwis started their innings strong with Latham and skipper Williamson scoring a ton and 91 respectively. However, Zimbabwe didn't take it lying down and pushed back later in the day. Masakadza got the breakthrough, removing Latham and captain Cremer followed it up with Williamson's scalp. The end of the innings saw Tiripano use the new ball to his advantage to take out Nicholls.
...Day 3, Session 1...

The Kiwis are on top here with a lead of 151 runs and they would look to add more from their middle order. Let's see how the hosts respond tomorrow. Zimbabwe bowled well today but the Kiwi batters were just good enough. Should be another fine day of Test cricket on day 3 so do join us to catch all the action. Cheers!

Graeme Cremer needs to regroup his team and bring in some plans for the post-Lunch session. Join us in a bit.

Pitch Report - There are damages done on the pitch. The city end of the pitch has grass and a bit of more bare area. The spinners can be benefited by bowling here. Seeing the marks on the pitch, one can bowl towards it to get a few wickets. Overall, the ball will keep low for pace bowling and will definitely allow the batsmen to score runs.

Today, it is going to be a test for the hosts on how they pan out their plans on bowling to the visiting side. Makhaya Ntini will surely want his side to bowl to their strengths and make a match out of it. Do join us at this beautiful stadium with a sporting pitch to play at it. Stay tuned.

Hello and a warm welcome for the first Test between New Zealand and Zimbabwe at the Queens Sports Club, Bulawayo. The hosts have been bowled out for a paltry total of 164 yesterday itself. They were falling like nine pins as they were not in a frame to play the consistent bouncers and good lengths of the Kiwi pace attack. Southee and Santner picked a wicket apiece but the star bowler was Neil Wagner who took his career-best figure of 6/41. Apart from Masvaure and Tripano nobody showed a stomach to fight. The New Zealand openers played really cautiously at the end of the day 1 with being 32/0.
...Day 2, Session 1...

As some ice packs are passed around in the home side's dressing room, Graeme Cremer will have to sit down with his boys and discuss the gameplan for tomorrow, about how they're going to go about their business against the visitors. The pitch is going to get flatter and turn quite a lot. Will be interesting to see how Day 2 pans out. Join us tomorrow at 1300 IST for all the action. Till then, later.
